correctness.rationale: The antecedent Krattenthaler–Müller Theorem 17 gives T_n≡1+2s₂(floor(n/2))+4e₂(n) mod8. Write n=2^(t+1)H+2^t−1, t=v₂(n+1); direct carry counting gives Δ(a,b)=(0,H mod2) for t=0 and (t mod2,(H+t−1) mod2) for t≥1. Every initial-state/low-bit triple is asymptotically uniformly distributed with O(√M) discrepancy by binary Walsh inversion and a signed 2×2 transfer with M_u M_u^T=2I. The parity-class trailing-run weights are t=0:1/2, positive odd t:1/3, positive even t:1/6; with conditional fair Δb this yields each 1/12 or 1/24 joint transition. Sum O(√(N/2^t)) over t gives O(√N) for every cutoff. A Rudin–Shapiro transfer shows B_r=∑_{n<2^r}(−1)^{e₂(n)}=2^ceil(r/2), a signed row-combination obstruction to a uniform smaller error exponent. Independent recurrence and digit checks verified first 514 coefficients and pair tables through 2^16; this does not substitute for infinite proof.

value.rationale: Consecutive residues of a classical integer sequence have a natural 16-state joint distribution; the exact two-level Markov-like transition probabilities show persistent dependence despite uniform one-point frequencies. A sharp all-cutoff square-root error and its obstruction supply mathematically reusable quantitative digit-correlation information, not merely rephrasing the antecedent digit formula.

final_claim: For every ordered j,k∈{1,3,5,7}, #{0≤n<N:T_n≡j,T_(n+1)≡k mod8}=N/12+O(√N) if α(j)=α(k) and N/24+O(√N) otherwise, α(j)=((j−1)/2) mod2. Both positive conditional probability tiers are exact; the √N exponent cannot be uniformly improved for the 16-pair family.
limitations: An earlier block-frequency theorem for the automatic sequence implicit in Theorem 17 might entail the same joint table; not categorically excluded.
